review_note: Reviewed 2026-10-22 from eight completed all-valence CASCI probes and user-supplied native natural-orbital AO coefficients at 2 and 30 angstrom in avdz-f12 and avtz-f12. Select the 2 angstrom source indices 8,12,13,14: the sulfur p-type lone-pair donor (two electrons) and the CH sigma/frontier-pair subspace (three electrons). The donor is source 8 at 2 angstrom but source 7 at 30 angstrom; these are geometry-specific indices, not a common energy window. Near selected occupations are 1.97918,1.48472,0.99467,0.50273 (DZ) and 1.97918,1.48447,0.99490,0.50297 (TZ). Far character-matched occupations are 1.99881,1.47041,0.76629,0.76595 (DZ) and 1.99881,1.47035,0.76637,0.76594 (TZ). Use four equally weighted doublet roots, as in the completed orbital screen, with D1 as the single reactive flux. Direct CASPT2-F12 energies use avdz-f12/avtz-f12 CBS with power 3.7 and the separately calculated 30 angstrom asymptote. The attempted auxiliary quartet CC/MR checks did not establish reference-state correspondence or CC quality; spin splitting is not used and the auxiliary quartet is removed from this newly installed model. The sulfur donor is selected by its 2 angstrom checkpoint identity and packed once, then propagated as a subspace, not reselected by ordinal at each geometry. Source 15 is mainly H2S S-H antibonding with occupation 0.08577/0.08553 at 2 angstrom, not the missing sulfur lone-pair donor. Its exclusion is a compact-space modeling choice, not demonstrated quantitative convergence; inspect S-H connectivity and orbital character in production and retain all scan-review guards. No optimized compact-CASSCF, correlated-potential, angular or asymptotic-plateau validation is claimed; the partial reference panel is diagnostic evidence and does not certify the direct potential. Production must retain native orbital, root and connectivity evidence for review.

states.energy_reference_note: One ground-parent adiabatic doublet path D1, referenced to its spin-free CH + H2S ground-fragment asymptote. The CH ground orbital pair is represented in the state average; it does not by itself establish a second reactive path into this well. Additional averaged roots are not extra flux; no claim that excited-path contributions vanish is implied.
